answer: Every slate is counted as it leaves the quarry bed, and the tally names the bed, the size and the man who split it. A orchard slate split on another hill fails the tally: at the haven of the roof the slates must match the quarry's own bed, and foreign slate weathers a different grey. Forging a tally means bribing the quarry master, faking a year of splittings and paying 14,500, and the sonnet record in the quarry office is read at every roofing, so a slate whose bed was never tallied is stripped.
